extracted.intended_audience: natural philosophers / chymists and educated readers engaged in chemical/experimental philosophy (early modern context)
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and methodological standards for judging claims about the 'elements' or 'principles' of mixed bodies — i.e., how to analyse compounds, what counts as an element, and how to interpret products of experimental operations (fire, reagents, putrefaction, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Specify kind and degree of fire used in analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: It were to be wish'd, our Chymists had clearly inform'd us what kinde of Division of Bodies by Fire must determine the number of the Elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Experiments must state whether the fire was open or applied in close vessels, and how violent or gentle the heat was. The text gives many examples: Guajacum yields ashes and soot in open fire but oil/spirit/vinegar/charcoal in retort; mild balneum separates unfermented blood into phlegme and caput mortuum while stronger heat yields spirits and oils; a further degree of heat may vitrify ashes into glass. Without specifying method/degree, different separations cannot be equated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish open-air vs closed-vessel effects
rubrics_metrics.description: As it is considerable in the Analysis of mixt Bodies, whether the Fire act on them when they are expos'd to the open Air, or shut up in close Vessels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open combustion and distillation in closed vessels produce different heterogeneities (e.g., camphire gives black unctuous soot from flame smoke but sublimes white in a closed vessel). The analytical claim must record the vessel conditions because conclusions about elements depend on them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require clear operational definition of what counts as an 'element' or 'principle'
rubrics_metrics.description: It may likewise be granted, that those distinct Substances, which Concretes generally either afford or are made up of, may without very much Inconvenience be call'd the Elements or Principles of them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must state whether 'element' means an ingredient not compound of anything further, or simply a constituent of mixed bodies. Beware of improprieties of speech; the definition affects which separations qualify as proving elemental status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not assume Fire is the universal analyzer
rubrics_metrics.description: It may reasonably enough be Doubted, how far, and in what sense, Fire ought to be esteem'd the genuine and universal Instrument of analyzing mixt Bodies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The critic should accept that other agents or methods (reagents, long digestion, alkalies, spirit of nitre, putrefaction, 'Alkahest') can separate substances that fire cannot. Examples: separation of gold/silver by reagents (aqua fortis) or antimony yielding sulphur after digestion with oil of vitriol. Analytical claims privileging fire must justify that privilege.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require consideration of alternative analytical means and reproducibility
rubrics_metrics.description: There are divers Separations to be made by other means, which either cannot at all, or else cannot so well be made by the Fire alone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyses should be reproducible with different valid techniques; if only one method yields a product, that product may be an artifact. The text gives procedures (digestion with oyl of vitriol, affusion of alkalizate salts) that produce separations fire alone does not.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish true elementary substances from de-compound or disguised products
rubrics_metrics.description: The pretended Salts and Sulphurs being so far from being Elementary parts extracted out of the Bodie of Mercurie, that they are rather ... De-compound Bodies, made up of the whole Metal and the Menstruum or other Additaments imploy'd to disguise it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claimed 'principles' must be examined rigorously to ensure they are not artifacts produced by added menstruums or process-induced recombinations. Use a 'skilful and rigid examen' to strip disguises and reveal if a product is merely a compound or an unchanged portion of the original metal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compare products obtained by different operations before declaring elemental status
rubrics_metrics.description: The Fire even when it divides a Body into Substances of divers Consistences, does not most commonly analyze it into Hypostatical Principles, but only disposes its parts into new Textures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If one operation yields oils/spirits/salts but another yields different heterogeneities, analysts must not assume the first set are true principles. The critic should test with multiple operations and see whether the same homogeneous substances repeatedly appear as separable components.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider the corpuscular explanation (bulk and figure of smallest parts) for variety
rubrics_metrics.description: If we assigne to the Corpuscles, whereof each Element consists, a peculiar size and shape, it may easily enough be manifested, That such differingly figur'd Corpuscles may be mingled in such various Proportions, and may be connected so many several wayes, that an almost incredible number of variously qualified Concretes may be compos'd of them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Theorists should account for diversity of compounds by properties of minute parts (size/shape) rather than assuming many distinct elemental substances; explanatory hypotheses should consider corpuscular structure implications for observed variety.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attend to fixation/resistance to fire as evidence about composition
rubrics_metrics.description: There are some mixt Bodies from which it has not been yet made appear, that any degree of Fire can separate either Salt or Sulphur or Mercury... The most obvious Instance of this Truth is Gold, which is a Body so fix'd ... that we finde not ... that it does discernably so much as lose of its fixednesse or weight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High resistance to decomposition by heat (e.g., gold's invariance under prolonged fusion) should be considered evidence that fire-based analysis fails to reveal components; this challenges assertions that fire can universally separate elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid equating separations with demonstration of elemental constitution
rubrics_metrics.description: Not only Chymists have not been able ... by Fire alone to separate true Sulphur from Antimony; ... the Productions of such Processes are Antimonial Sulphurs rather in Name than Nature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obtaining a named substance (e.g., 'sulphur') from a mineral does not alone prove it is a constituent in the elemental sense — show that the separated body is homogeneous, independent, and not generated by reaction with reagents or experimental conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for process-induced relocation of parts (evaporation, migration) versus chemical separation
rubrics_metrics.description: Some Bodies being of such a Texture that the Fire can drive them into the cooler and less hot part of the Vessels wherein they are included, and if need be, remove them from place to place to fly the greatest heat, more easily than it can divorce their Elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analysts must distinguish between components carried off by motion (sublimation, distillative migration) and components produced by genuine decomposition. E.g., soot migrating in a retort may give different products than direct burning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require attention to the effect of added reagents (affusion/alkalizates) in separations
rubrics_metrics.description: The Metalline part of Vitriol will not be so easily ... separated from the Saline part even by a violent Fire, as by the Affusion of certain Alkalizate Salts in a liquid Form upon the Solution of Vitriol made in common water.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reagents are used to precipitate or separate components, the role of those reagents in changing the substance's constitution must be analyzed: are they revealing pre-existing components, or creating new compounds that appear as separable parts?

rubrics_metrics.name: Include examples and counterexamples in methodological claims
rubrics_metrics.description: For if we assigne to the Corpuscles ... and how great a variety of Phænomena the same matter ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Methodological assertions should be supported by concrete experimental instances and counterinstances (the text supplies many: guajacum, camphire, brimstone, antimony, sal armoniack, etc.). Use such examples to test hypotheses about elemental constitution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize that mild or natural processes can reveal volatile components
rubrics_metrics.description: The Inflamable Spirit ... may not only be separated from [wine] by the gentle heat of a Bath, but may be distill'd either by the help of the Sun-Beams, or even of a Dunghill.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analysts must accept that slow, low-temperature, or biological processes (putrefaction, solar distillation) can liberate volatile components that are as 'element-like' as those separated by violent fire; methodological standards should include such processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language caution: acknowledge conventional naming vs ontological claim
rubrics_metrics.description: When I said, 'without very much Inconvenience', I had in my Thoughts that sober Admonition of Galen, 'Cum de re constat, de verbis non est Litigandum'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Writers and experimenters should be careful in naming (elements/principles) and separate terminological convenience from claims about ultimate ontological composition. Avoid letting words determine conclusions.
